hypotheses.title: Hydrogen Sulfide Donor SG1002 Extends Mouse Lifespan
hypotheses.claim: Administration of SG1002, a hydrogen sulfide donor, extends lifespan in Mus musculus. The intervention is expected to increase median and maximal lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Hydrogen sulfide participates in mitochondrial bioenergetics, vascular function, and cellular stress resistance. Controlled elevation of sulfide signaling could thereby slow age-related functional decline.
hypotheses.prediction: SG1002-treated mice will show significantly longer median and maximal lifespan than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of mice to SG1002 or vehicle and follow them for lifespan under identical conditions. Analyze survival curves with log-rank tests and adjust for sex and cage effects.

hypotheses.title: Rapamycin Shortens Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Administration of rapamycin shortens lifespan in Mus musculus. Treated mice are expected to show reduced median and maximal lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Rapamycin suppresses mTOR-dependent growth and repair processes. Persistent inhibition of these pathways could impair tissue maintenance and increase vulnerability to age-related damage.
hypotheses.prediction: Rapamycin-treated mice will show significantly shorter median and maximal lifespan than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of mice to rapamycin or vehicle and follow them for lifespan under identical conditions. Analyze survival curves with log-rank tests and adjust for sex and cage effects.

hypotheses.title: Rapamycin Extends Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Administration of rapamycin extends lifespan in Mus musculus. Treated mice are expected to show increased median and maximal lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Moderate attenuation of mTOR signaling reduces anabolic overdrive and enhances cellular housekeeping. Such metabolic modulation could delay the onset of multiple age-related pathologies.
hypotheses.prediction: Rapamycin-treated mice will show significantly longer median and maximal lifespan than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of mice to rapamycin or vehicle and follow them for lifespan under identical conditions. Analyze survival curves with log-rank tests and adjust for sex and cage effects.

hypotheses.title: Medium-Chain Triglyceride Oil Extends Mouse Lifespan
hypotheses.claim: Supplementation with medium-chain triglyceride oil extends lifespan in Mus musculus. Supplemented mice are expected to show increased median and maximal lifespan relative to controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Medium-chain triglycerides provide an efficiently metabolized energy source and can promote ketone production. Improved metabolic flexibility and mitochondrial fuel quality could support healthy aging.
hypotheses.prediction: Mice receiving medium-chain triglyceride oil will show significantly longer median and maximal lifespan than controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of mice to medium-chain triglyceride oil or isocaloric control diet and follow them for lifespan under identical conditions. Analyze survival curves with log-rank tests and adjust for sex and cage effects.

hypotheses.title: Chlorpromazine Extends Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Administration of chlorpromazine extends lifespan in Mus musculus. Treated mice are expected to show increased median and maximal lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Chlorpromazine modulates membrane properties, autophagy, and inflammatory signaling. These cellular effects could reduce chronic damage accumulation and slow the progression of age-related decline.
hypotheses.prediction: Chlorpromazine-treated mice will show significantly longer median and maximal lifespan than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of mice to chlorpromazine or vehicle and follow them for lifespan under identical conditions. Analyze survival curves with log-rank tests and adjust for sex and cage effects.

hypotheses.title: Chlorpromazine Shortens Lifespan in Mus musculus
hypotheses.claim: Administration of chlorpromazine shortens lifespan in Mus musculus. Treated mice are expected to show reduced median and maximal lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Chlorpromazine interferes with dopaminergic signaling, mitochondrial function, and cellular membranes. Chronic exposure to such perturbations could accelerate tissue dysfunction and increase mortality risk.
hypotheses.prediction: Chlorpromazine-treated mice will show significantly shorter median and maximal lifespan than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Randomize a large cohort of mice to chlorpromazine or vehicle and follow them for lifespan under identical conditions. Analyze survival curves with log-rank tests and adjust for sex and cage effects.

hypotheses.title: Rapamycin Extends Lifespan via mTORC1 Activation
hypotheses.claim: Rapamycin extends lifespan in Mus musculus by activating mTORC1 signaling. The lifespan benefit depends mechanistically on increased mTORC1 pathway activity in treated mice.
hypotheses.rationale: mTORC1 integrates nutrient signals to regulate growth, autophagy, and metabolism. Engagement of this pathway by rapamycin could trigger adaptive responses that preserve tissue function during aging.
hypotheses.prediction: Lifespan extension in rapamycin-treated mice will correlate with elevated mTORC1 signaling markers and be abolished when mTORC1 activation is blocked.
hypotheses.experiment: Treat mice with rapamycin alone, rapamycin plus an mTORC1 pathway inhibitor, or vehicle, and measure lifespan alongside mTORC1 activity. Compare survival and pathway readouts across groups to test mechanistic dependence.
